Abstract: We cycled symmetric lithium metal cells on GZ-9 separators at stack pressures of 1, 5 and 10 MPa and a current density of 0.2 mA cm-2 at 25 °C.

Finding: at 5 MPa, GZ-9 cells cycled stably for 200 cycles before the study ended, with no short circuit. At 10 MPa, two of three cells short-circuited within 40 cycles. At 1 MPa, voids formed at the lithium interface and the overpotential doubled within 50 cycles.
